gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, normalised against Intel's own memory ceilings, the TerraMaster F2-425 Plus's advertised 32 GB RAM maximum is double what Intel rates the N150 for (16 GB), while the Synology DS225+'s 6 GB ceiling equals Immich's stated 6 GB minimum and sits below Immich's 8 GB recommendation, so only the N100/N150 units reach Immich's recommended RAM on a maker-backed figure.
standout_why: Compared against homelabwise.com (gives UGREEN/Synology RAM maxes but no Intel ceiling or Immich requirement), nasdecoded.com (maker RAM maxes only, no power or HA detail), bitdoze.com (no RAM max for DXP2800, no HAOS-vs-Container distinction), starryhope.com (lists 32 GB for F2-425 Plus unchallenged; says UGREEN permits TrueNAS/Unraid but nothing on stock VM support). None of them put the maker RAM ceiling next to Intel's ARK figure, none quote Immich's own 6 GB minimum / 8 GB recommended, and none say that Home Assistant Container lacks Apps (add-ons) and one-click updates so the shopper needs a VM-capable NAS OS to get full Home Assistant. Dealectric's current page also lacks all three.
decides: Confirms the UGREEN DXP2800 as the pick and narrows the gap the F2-425 Plus appeared to have: on Intel-rated memory both top out at 16 GB (single channel, one slot), so the TerraMaster's 32 GB is a maker claim beyond the CPU spec, not a verified advantage. Rules the Synology DS225+ out for Immich with machine learning: its 6 GB hard ceiling meets only Immich's minimum and leaves nothing for a Home Assistant OS VM. The HA finding (Container has no Apps/add-ons or one-click updates; HAOS is built for VMs) means the shopper should buy a NAS whose stock OS runs VMs: Synology lists 2 recommended VM instances on the DS225+ and Asustor lists VirtualBox as an official app for the AS5402T; UGREEN's and TerraMaster's own VM pages could not be opened this session.

findings.value: 16 GB, 1 memory channel, Quick Sync Video yes, 6 W TDP
findings.note: Intel notes the max is 'dependent on memory type'. This is the ceiling for the UGREEN DXP2800.

findings.label: Intel N150 maximum memory (CPU vendor)

findings.note: Ceiling for the TerraMaster F2-425 Plus and Beelink ME mini. TerraMaster's advertised 32 GB (as reported on starryhope.com) is 2x Intel's figure; treat 16 GB as the vendor-backed ceiling.

findings.note: Synology caps the DS225+ at 6 GB, 2 GB below the CPU's rated 8 GB, because 2 GB is soldered and the single slot takes a 4 GB module.

findings.label: Immich hardware requirements
findings.value: RAM minimum 6 GB, recommended 8 GB (4 GB only with machine learning disabled); CPU 2 cores minimum, 4 recommended; ML container needs x86-64-v2 on amd64; Postgres on local SSD, never a network share
findings.note: Postgres needs at least 2 GB if Docker limits are set. This is the yardstick for the RAM column.

findings.label: Home Assistant Container vs Home Assistant OS
findings.value: Container has no Apps (add-ons), no out-of-the-box Thread/Z-Wave, no one-click updates; HA OS is designed for single-board computers or virtual machines
findings.note: So a Docker-only NAS gives a reduced Home Assistant; full HA needs a NAS OS that runs VMs.
